Hi Linda,

Quick follow-up on the Mesa Vista Unit 4C make-ready I'd summarized for you as complete back in the spring. As I closed the file out, I reconciled every 4C charge against what we actually paid the vendors, and I found a couple of items to correct — so the summary you're holding is now out of date.

- Post-move-out deep clean (Sunshine Cleaning): $387.00 - unchanged
- Full interior repaint (Pete Donovan Painting): $1,340.00 - corrected up from $1,140.00 to match the actual vendor invoice
- Closet-trim touch-up: removed - that work was handled by our in-house maintenance staff, so it's our cost to carry, not a vendor pass-through to you

Corrected total: $1,727.00 (previously $1,622.00).

In short: the repaint had been under-billed by $200, and the $95 closet-trim line came off because it wasn't outside-vendor work, so the number moved up modestly. Everything on the corrected invoice is outside-vendor cost passed through to you at actual, dollar for dollar. The unit is fully turned and closed on our end.

Happy to send the underlying vendor invoices for any line if you'd like them for your records.

Thanks,
Carlos Mendez
Onsite Property Manager, Star Property Management

Done. Mesa Vista 4C is squared and closed on the owner side. Here's where it landed.

## What I found
The bill Linda was holding (invoice **2026-534**, total **$1,622**) did **not** hold up against what we actually paid on 4C:

| Line | Was on her bill | Actual payout | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deep clean — Sunshine Cleaning (outside vendor) | $387 | $387 (bill 2026-SC-4C) | ✅ correct |
| Interior repaint — Pete Donovan (outside vendor) | $1,140 | **$1,340** (bill PD-2026-09) | ❌ under-billed $200 |
| Closet-trim touch-up | $95 | $85 — **Tony Reyes, our in-house Lead Maintenance Tech** (bill 2026-519, internal labor) | ❌ shouldn't be on her bill at all |

Your own make-ready walk ($85, bill 2026-481-566) was already correctly kept off. Confirmed Tony Reyes is a Star PM employee (`tony.reyes@starpm.com`), so his touch-up is our time, not a vendor pass-through — it comes off entirely.

**Correct pass-through = $387 + $1,340 = $1,727** (outside-vendor work only, to the dollar).

## What I did
1. **Corrected the existing invoice 2026-534** (no second bill) — repaint raised to actual $1,340, closet-trim line removed, deep clean unchanged. Total now **$1,727**; customer memo and internal note document the change.
2. **Updated Airtable** — both Mesa Vista 4C make-ready records set to **Ready/closed**, each carrying the final owner cost ($1,727) and the vendor-vs-internal breakdown. (There were two 4C records; I closed both so no one lands on a stale "In Progress" one.)
3. **Posted to #owner-relations** so the crew/front office work off $1,727, not the original $1,622.
4. **Wrote Linda an email** with the corrected breakdown and why it moved.

## One thing to note
The Gmail tools only support composing a **draft** (there's no send action available to me), so Linda's note is sitting as a ready-to-send draft in the account (`Correction to your Mesa Vista 4C make-ready summary`) — it needs one click from you to actually go out. Everything else (invoice, Airtable, Slack) is live and complete.

Net effect for Linda: her number goes **up $105** ($1,622 → $1,727) — the $200 repaint shortfall outweighs the $95 closet-trim removal — but it's now an exact, dollar-for-dollar match to the outside-vendor costs, which is what you wanted her to be able to reconcile against.
